ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AD=1, AB=2\sqrt{2}$, $M$ is a moving point on line segment $BD$, $MP\perp CD$ at point $P$, $MQ\perp BC$ at point $Q$, what is the minimum value of $PQ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect CM as shown in the figure,\\
$ \because MP\perp CD$ at point P, $MQ\perp BC$ at point Q,\\
$ \therefore \angle CPM=\angle CQM=90^\circ$,\\
$ \because $ quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
$ \therefore BC=AD=1, CD=AB=2\sqrt{2}$, $ \angle BCD=90^\circ$,\\
$ \therefore $ quadrilateral PCQM is a rectangle,\\
$ \therefore PQ=CM$,\\
In $ \triangle BCD$, $BD=\sqrt{BC^{2}+CD^{2}}=\sqrt{1^{2}+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}=3$,\\
When CM $ \perp $BD, CM is minimized, then PQ is minimized,\\
At this time, $ S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}BD\cdot CM=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot CD$,\\
$ \therefore CM=\frac{BC\cdot CD}{BD}=\frac{1\times 2\sqrt{2}}{3}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$,\\
$ \therefore PQ$'s minimum value is $ \boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is rectangle ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, D is at the upper left; diagonal BD connects from D to B, and moving point M is located on line segment BD. Through M draw a vertical line intersecting CD at P, that is, MP is perpendicular to CD; through M draw a horizontal line intersecting BC at Q, that is, MQ is perpendicular to BC. In the figure, P, C, Q, M form a small rectangle PCQM, and the small-rectangle diagonal relationship corresponding to PQ is drawn. Reasoning: In rectangle ABCD, AD=1, AB=2√2, so BC=AD=1, CD=AB=2√2, and ∠BCD=90°. Since MP⊥CD, MQ⊥BC, and CD⊥BC, PCQM is a rectangle. In rectangle PCQM, the diagonals are equal, therefore PQ=CM. Thus finding the minimum value of PQ is equivalent to finding the minimum value of CM when M moves on line segment BD. In right triangle BCD, BC=1, CD=2√2, so BD=√(BC^2+CD^2)=√(1^2+(2√2)^2)=√9=3. The shortest distance from point C to line BD is the perpendicular segment; when CM⊥BD, CM is minimal. Expressed using the area of triangle BCD: 1/2·BD·CM = 1/2·BC·CD, so CM=(BC·CD)/BD=(1·2√2)/3=2√2/3. Because PQ=CM, the minimum value of PQ is 2√2/3.
